newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end mixed, gold sees gains.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end mixed, gold sees gains.

text.p: New York precious metals ended mixed in fairly light volume but gold and silver's technical health looked slightly better despite producer selling paring gains in the yellow metal, traders said.
Greg Drury of Mitsui and Co said producer selling of gold above the market was still a concern.
"Producers continue to be seriously underhedged," Drury said.
April COMEX gold settled $1.00 firmer at $347.70 an ounce, traded $348.80 to $346.10. Bullion was quoted by dealers at $345.60 to $346.10.

Traders said that gold and silver's technical outlook was a little improved following gold's gains from last week's contract low, and silver's close Tuesday above $5.20 an ounce in the March COMEX contract, along with a healthy increase in silver's open interest.
March silver settled 3.7 cents weaker at $5.215 an ounce, traded $5.255 to $5.19.
Merrill Lynch said in its latest bi-weekly commodity outlook that it still forecast a steady erosion of gold prices, but a further advance in palladium.
"The dollar has been and continues to be a major enemy of gold bulls," Merrill Lynch said. It recently lowered its downside gold price objective by $10 to $320 for spot metal.
NYMEX April platinum ended lower in choppy trading, pulling back from the day's lows twice before closing 60 cents weaker at $371.40 an ounce, traded $374.50 to $369.50.
NYMEX March palladium went out 25 cents firmer at $137.00 an ounce.
"The rest of the precious metals complex seems to be divorcing itself, at least to some degree, from gold," Merrill Lynch said.

Palladium sponge supplies could remain tight for a few more weeks until the Russians, the world's biggest producer, complete their negotiations to sell material to the Japanese who represent 40 percent of world demand, Merrill added.
Earlier traders in Tokyo said until a negotiation schedule between the Japanese and Russians was clearer, bullish sentiment in palladium would continue.
